page.layout: One column of running text, left of the page. Running head at the top right with the page number 133. No marginal notes. Signature "i 3" and catchword "ti" at the foot.

main_text.p: tum: hoc eft,quatuor habue-rat pro decē. emptor igitur tum deceptus dicitur, cū rei precium dimidio ampliusau[?]ctum eft: hoc eft, cum fexde-cim perfoluta funt. Intentio: Deceptus fum fupra dimi-dium ueri precij. D.Nō es de-ceptus. Q. An fit? R. Quia pe-cunia tua non fuperat altero tanto rem meam: hoc eft, ut pinguius loquamur, non ua-let duplo plus quàm res mea. tum enim deceptus esses, si res mea non ualeret dimidiū tuæ pecuniæ. F. At mea pecu-nia ultra uerum rei precium, ualet plus dimidio precij tuæ rei. nam & decem dedi, quã-

page.notes: The running head letters overlap and are blurred; "IVRIS CONSVLTVS" is my best reading. "ampliusau[?]ctum" is uncertain: the word after "ampliusau" looks like "ctum" with a damaged first letter, possibly "auctum". The signature reads "i 3", and the catchword "ti" is a fragment that begins the next page's word.
